hero.title: Tripitaka: The Three Baskets
hero.description: The foundational scriptural canon of Theravada Buddhism, representing the oral teachings of the Buddha compiled through early councils.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Structure

  • Vinaya: Discipline
  • Sutta: Discourses
  • Abhidhamma: Philosophy

Key Figures

  • Upali: Expert in Vinaya
  • Ananda: Expert in Sutta
  • Mahakassapa: Led 1st Council

The Three Pillars

  • Vinaya Pitaka: Code of conduct for Monks (Bhikkhus) and Nuns (Bhikkhunis). Includes Patimokkha rules.
  • Sutta Pitaka: Largest collection; Buddha’s sermons, dialogues, and Jataka tales.
  • Abhidhamma Pitaka: Systematic, scholastic analysis of Buddhist doctrines, meta-psychology.
PitakaFocusKey Components
VinayaConductSutta-vibhanga, Khandhaka, Parivara
SuttaDoctrineDigha, Majjhima, Samyutta, Anguttara, Khuddaka
AbhidhammaAnalysisDhammasangani, Kathavatthu, etc.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The evolution of the Pali Canon from oral tradition to written text.

cards.details: Held at Rajgriha under Ajatashatru; compilation of Vinaya and Sutta began.
Held at Vaishali; initial signs of doctrinal division (Sthaviras vs Mahasanghikas).
Tripitaka written down on palm leaves at Aluvihara under King Vattagamani Abhaya.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing Abhidhamma Pitaka with early teachings; it was a later addition (3rd Council).
Assuming Tripitakas were written down immediately after Buddha's death (they were oral for centuries).
Thinking all Tripitakas are in Sanskrit; they are traditionally in Pali (Theravada).
